title: Dataflow Gen2 Error 20302: A Misleading 'User Configuration Issue' Message
summary: A community troubleshooting note on Dataflow Gen2 error code 20302, a generic 'user configuration issue' message that the post argues actually masks either a stale owner identity or a CI/CD deployment defaulting the dataflow's type property to a legacy value.
audience: Data engineers running Dataflow Gen2 refreshes on a schedule, especially teams deploying dataflows through CI/CD pipelines rather than the Fabric UI.
why_it_matters: Error 20302's generic wording gives no indication of the two very different underlying causes the post identifies, so knowing both failure modes up front (identity/ownership vs. a deployment-time type mismatch) narrows troubleshooting substantially.
takeaways: Error 20302 during scheduled Dataflow Gen2 refresh is described as a generic message that can stem from unrelated root causes.
One cause is the dataflow being bound to a creator's credentials that later become invalid (departure, password change).
Another cause is CI/CD-deployed dataflows defaulting to a legacy 'Dataflow' type property instead of 'Dataflow Fabric'.
The post's suggested fix for the type-mismatch case is to explicitly set the dataflow type property in the deployed pipeline JSON.

claims.text: Dataflow Gen2 error code 20302 surfaces with the generic message 'user configuration issue' during scheduled refresh, which the post describes as masking an underlying identity or definition problem rather than pointing to a specific misconfiguration.

One reported cause of error 20302 is that a Dataflow Gen2 refresh is bound to the identity/credentials of the dataflow's creator, so the refresh begins failing if that person leaves the organization or their password changes.

The post recommends taking explicit ownership of the dataflow in its settings and forcing a metadata refresh (e.g. editing a step description or renaming a Power Query step, then republishing) as a fix for the stale-identity cause of error 20302.

A second reported cause of error 20302 is CI/CD-deployed pipeline definitions defaulting the dataflow's type property to the legacy 'Dataflow' value instead of the Gen2-specific 'Dataflow Fabric' value, which the post identifies as case-sensitive.

The post's suggested fix for the CI/CD type-mismatch cause is to edit the deployed pipeline activity's JSON definition and explicitly set the dataflowType property to 'Dataflow Fabric' rather than relying on the deployment tool's default.

As a preventive measure, the post recommends including the dataflowType property explicitly in source-controlled ARM/pipeline templates and using a stable service account, rather than an individual employee's identity, as the dataflow owner.
